Output_Decision: Evaluate CPU demand under the actual target concurrency/load scenario.

Limitations: Does not provide a universal concurrency-to-core equation.

Rule_Name: Latency-Sensitive Inference Requires CPU-Side Latency Contribution Assessment
Rule_Description: When inference is latency-sensitive, CPU-side request/input/output/handler time shall be measured or otherwise isolated where possible instead of assuming that model compute alone represents end-to-end latency.
Inputs: End-to-end request latency; queue time; input processing; model compute; output processing; handler overhead
Condition: Workload has a latency-sensitive inference objective
Threshold_Value: Use workload SLA/target from Inference Rules; no universal CPU threshold
Output_Decision: Include measurable CPU-side contribution in latency analysis and flag CPU as a constraint if evidence links it to target violation.
Exact_Source_Title: Triton Server Trace
Page_Section_Table_Equation: Trace Summary Tool; HTTP/GRPC request breakdown
Evidence: Triton trace decomposes request handling into receive/send, overhead, queue, compute, input and output components, enabling CPU-side/serving contributions to be examined rather than treating model inference as the entire request.
Limitations: Trace components are serving-stack measurements; exact CPU attribution may require system profiling.
Consolidation_Note: Related to CPU-P5-08; retained because Part 4 defines latency contribution measurement and Part 5 applies it to feasibility.

Rule_Name: Batch Inference CPU Assessment Must Preserve Batch Context
Rule_Description: For batch/offline inference, CPU requirement measurements shall preserve batch size and execution configuration because request and execution counts can differ under batching.
Inputs: Batch size; request count; inference count; execution count; CPU processing measurements
Condition: Inference uses explicit or dynamic batching
Threshold_Value: Actual batch configuration; no universal batch size
Output_Decision: Compare CPU demand using the same batch configuration used for the benchmark/workload target.
Exact_Source_Title: Metrics — NVIDIA Triton Inference Server
Page_Section_Table_Equation: Inference Request Metrics; Counts
Evidence: Triton documents that request count, inference count and execution count differ under batching and can be used to interpret average batch size.
Limitations: This preserves benchmark context; it does not define a universal CPU cost per batch.

Rule_Name: Training and Inference CPU Rules Must Not Be Symmetrically Duplicated
Rule_Description: A CPU rule shall be created for training or inference only when the CPU-specific mechanism is distinct and evidence-supported; workload labels alone are insufficient.
Inputs: CPU mechanism; workload stage; source evidence
Input_Source: Parts 1–3; training/inference resource rules; authoritative documentation
Condition: A proposed training-vs-inference distinction is under consideration
Output_Decision: Keep only genuinely distinct CPU-specific requirements; otherwise reference the existing generic CPU rule.
Exact_Source_Title: DALI Documentation; Triton Metrics Documentation
Page_Section_Table_Equation: DALI data processing pipelines; Triton inference request metrics
Evidence: NVIDIA documentation demonstrates different CPU-relevant mechanisms in training/data pipelines versus serving/request handling, while not supporting arbitrary fixed CPU requirements for each workload class.
Limitations: This is a catalogue-governance rule; it does not assert that all training/inference workloads differ.
Validation_Status: B — derived from source-supported distinct mechanisms and catalogue boundary.

Rule_Name: CPU Compute Feasibility Requires Demand-Capacity Comparison
Rule_Description: A candidate CPU is compute-feasible when validated CPU processing demand can be supported by the candidate capacity under the evaluated configuration.
Inputs: Required equivalent CPU core demand; candidate CPU_Cores; candidate CPU_Threads; workload configuration
Condition: Validated CPU-side demand has been quantified
Output_Decision: PASS if capacity supports demand; otherwise CPU compute constraint
Exact_Source_Title: CPU Metrics Reference
Page_Section_Table_Equation: Average Physical Core Utilization; Average Logical Core Utilization; Back-End Bound
Evidence: Intel provides physical/logical utilization and explains core/memory-bound execution. The DSS comparison consumes the measured demand representation established in Part 1.
Limitations: Core/thread counts are capacity descriptors, not a universal workload-performance model.
Validation_Status: B — derived from Part 1 measured demand and authoritative CPU metrics.

Rule_Name: CPU Thread Feasibility Must Preserve Configured Parallelism
Rule_Description: When CPU demand is represented in configured threads, candidate CPU thread capacity shall be compared with required configured thread demand.
Inputs: Required CPU threads; CPU_Threads; pipeline/serving parallelism
Condition: CPU stage is explicitly configured or measured in parallel threads
Output_Decision: PASS if configured thread capacity supports demand; otherwise thread constraint
Exact_Source_Title: Pipeline and processing graph
Page_Section_Table_Equation: num_threads; exec_pipelined
Evidence: DALI defines num_threads as the number of CPU threads used by the pipeline.
Limitations: Configured thread count does not guarantee throughput; no universal conversion is assumed.
Validation_Status: A — directly supported for configured pipeline threads.

Rule_Name: CPU Data-Pipeline Bottleneck Requires Downstream Impact Evidence
Rule_Description: Flag a CPU data pipeline as a bottleneck only when insufficient CPU-side processing is linked to inability to sustain downstream consumption or observed performance loss.
Inputs: Required pipeline throughput; validated CPU pipeline throughput; downstream consumption; observed waiting/starvation
Input_Source: Part 2; DALI bottleneck detection; workload profiling
Condition: CPU pipeline capacity is below demand or profiling shows CPU-induced waiting/performance loss
Threshold_Value: Pipeline capacity < workload demand with corroborating impact
Output_Decision: Flag CPU data-pipeline bottleneck; otherwise do not label CPU bottleneck
Exact_Source_Title: Data Loading Bottleneck Detection
Page_Section_Table_Equation: Overview; Identify if data loading is the bottleneck
Evidence: NVIDIA provides a workflow to identify whether data loading slows training and whether the GPU waits for data.
Limitations: High CPU utilization alone is insufficient.

Rule_Name: CPU Memory-Bandwidth Feasibility Uses Validated Sustained Bandwidth
Rule_Description: Flag a CPU memory-bandwidth constraint when workload demand exceeds validated sustained bandwidth available to the relevant configuration.
Inputs: Required workload memory bandwidth; validated sustained CPU memory bandwidth
Condition: CPU stage is memory-bandwidth-sensitive
Output_Decision: Flag bandwidth constraint; otherwise bandwidth-feasible
Exact_Source_Title: CPU Metrics Reference
Page_Section_Table_Equation: Memory Bandwidth; Memory Bound; DRAM Bandwidth Bound
Evidence: Intel documents memory-bandwidth and memory-bound diagnostics; feasibility uses validated sustained bandwidth rather than a specification value.
Limitations: No safety margin is assumed.
Validation_Status: B — derived from Part 3 and Intel diagnostics.

Rule_Name: CPU Memory-Bandwidth Bottleneck Requires Performance Evidence
Rule_Description: High bandwidth activity shall not alone be labeled a bottleneck; profiling must support a performance-limiting relationship.
Inputs: Memory Bound; DRAM Bandwidth Bound; application performance; timeline
Condition: Memory-bandwidth pressure is observed
Output_Decision: Flag only when profiling supports performance limitation
Exact_Source_Title: CPU Metrics Reference
Page_Section_Table_Equation: Memory Bandwidth; Memory Bound; DRAM Bandwidth Bound
Evidence: Intel identifies stalls and heavy DRAM bandwidth use as diagnostics and recommends deeper memory analysis.
Limitations: Tool thresholds/histograms are configuration dependent.

Rule_Name: Training CPU Bottleneck Must Be Tied to Pipeline Performance
Rule_Description: For training, CPU is a bottleneck only when loading/preprocessing/tokenization limitations are linked to reduced training pipeline performance or downstream accelerator waiting.
Inputs: Training pipeline throughput; CPU stage timing; downstream consumption; waiting/starvation evidence
Input_Source: Part 4; DALI bottleneck detection; training profiling
Condition: CPU-side training stage limits or interrupts required flow
Output_Decision: Flag training CPU bottleneck only with causal workload evidence
Exact_Source_Title: Data Loading Bottleneck Detection
Page_Section_Table_Equation: Overview; Identify if data loading is the bottleneck
Evidence: NVIDIA provides a workflow to determine whether data loading slows training and whether GPU waiting for data occurs.
Limitations: No universal utilization/core threshold.

Rule_Name: Inference CPU Bottleneck Must Be Linked to Serving Performance
Rule_Description: For inference, CPU is a bottleneck only when CPU-side request/input/output/serving work is linked to degraded throughput, latency, queueing, or another defined serving-performance loss.
Inputs: CPU metrics; request latency; queue time; compute-input/output time; throughput; concurrency
Condition: CPU-side serving demand correlates with serving degradation
Output_Decision: Flag inference CPU bottleneck when measured CPU contribution is causally linked to serving constraint
Exact_Source_Title: Metrics — NVIDIA Triton Inference Server
Page_Section_Table_Equation: Latency; CPU Metrics; Request/Queue/Compute metrics
Evidence: Triton exposes request, queue, compute-input/output timing and CPU metrics.
Limitations: CPU attribution may require system profiling.

Rule_Name: Latency-Sensitive CPU Feasibility Uses CPU-Side Latency Contribution
Rule_Description: For latency-sensitive inference, CPU feasibility shall consider measured CPU/serving-side latency contribution in the context of the existing workload latency target.
Inputs: CPU-side latency; workload latency target; request/queue/processing timings
Condition: Latency target exists and CPU-side timing can be isolated
Threshold_Value: Use workload-specific target; no universal CPU share
Output_Decision: Flag CPU constraint only if CPU contribution prevents target satisfaction and evidence supports causality
Exact_Source_Title: Triton Server Trace
Page_Section_Table_Equation: Trace Summary Tool; request/queue/compute/input/output components
Evidence: Triton tracing provides request-component timing for latency decomposition.
Limitations: Trace components are not all pure CPU time.
Validation_Status: B — derived from source-supported measurements and workload target.

Rule_Name: CPU Feasibility Is the Conjunction of Applicable CPU Constraints
Rule_Description: A candidate CPU is CPU-feasible only when every applicable CPU-specific constraint passes: compute, configured thread capacity, pipeline throughput, memory bandwidth, and serving/processing demand where applicable.
Inputs: Applicable CPU feasibility checks from Parts 1–5
Condition: All applicable CPU constraints evaluated
Output_Decision: CPU_FEASIBLE = TRUE only if all applicable checks pass; otherwise CPU_CONSTRAINED
Exact_Source_Title: CPU Metrics Reference; NVIDIA DALI Documentation; Triton Metrics
Page_Section_Table_Equation: CPU Metrics; DALI pipelines; Triton metrics
Evidence: Sources provide distinct compute, memory, pipeline and serving measurements; the AND decision is DSS-derived.
Limitations: No weighted score or safety margin. Final decision semantics require supervisor approval.
Validation_Status: B/D — derived DSS composition; supervisor approval required.
